title: The $c_3$ mass gap and continuum hyperbolic geometry: the $\pi/3$ Lobachevsky saddle as geometric envelope
html:
Remark. The c_3 mass gap and continuum hyperbolic geometry: the \pi/3 Lobachevsky saddle as geometric envelope

The third topological mass gap observable c_3 was initially measured via empirical extrapolation of the N=3 operator-valued calculations across the Q_\beta manifold, resulting in a near-match physical measurement of:

 c_3^{\text{emp}} \approx -2.02162

The canonical q = 1 shadow of this quantity is J_{\text{Hopf}}(1) = -2 (kernel-constraint registry KC10/KC20, C_{\text{Hopf}}(2) = -2). The question addressed below is whether the residual gap between c_3^{\text{emp}} and -2 admits a continuum-geometric description. (Combinatorial constraints proposed over S_5 cells did not survive scrutiny.)

The Continuum Limit Kashaev Integral

By transitioning to the full continuous Faddeev non-compact integration \Phi_b(z) over the analytic contour \mathbb{R} + i\delta, the operator expansion is replaced entirely by the thermodynamic saddle point of the continuum potential.

For the ground-state 4_1 (figure-eight pion) topology, the non-compact potential transforms exactly into the imaginary part of the quantum dilogarithm:

 V(\theta) = \text{Im}(\text{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}))

The Saddle Point Construction

The critical saddle point of the continuous action sits at \theta = \pi/3, where the potential evaluates to the volume of a regular ideal tetrahedron (V(\pi/3) \approx 1.01494) and the two-tetrahedron gluing of the 4_1 complement gives the total macroscopic physical action \text{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.02988; the saddle derivation is carried out once in the dilog saddle regime.

The asymptotic bound (scope-limited)

The full non-perturbative Kashaev invariant (calculated via high-precision Borel–Padé extrapolation across N \in [1000, 2050]) pins the topological action of the geometric envelope:

 A = \frac{\text{Vol}(4_1)}{\pi} \approx 0.6461318

The candidate identification

 c_3 \xrightarrow{N \to \infty} -\text{Vol}(4_1) \approx -2.02988

is scope-limited, not exact: -\text{Vol}(4_1) is anchor-blind, missing both substrate anchors (muon +0.479\%, proton -1.907\%) while the measured c_3 itself swings 2.43\% across anchors (muon -2.0202, proton -2.0693); at the muon (CAL-2) pin it is 6.9\times worse than the precision-ladder near-match -\text{Vol}(4_1) + u - (10/3)\,u^2. The residual between the observed -2.0216 and -2.02988 was previously attributed to finite-size truncation scaling; the cross-anchor swing shows the identification itself does not close.

What stands is the hyperbolic geometry: \text{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3), with the Lobachevsky saddle at \theta = \pi/3, supplies the geometric envelope that anchor-sensitive corrections (the precision ladder) refine — not a rigorous continuum evaluation of c_3.

Every c_3 figure quoted above is stated in the convention-C frame, z = \sqrt{q}/(q+1). The canonical Markov parameter is convention D, z = q^3/(q^2+1), under which the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder has not been re-derived; the figures are correct as recorded and are scoped, not corrected. The hyperbolic geometry — \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3), with the saddle at \theta = \pi/3 — is convention-independent and is unaffected.
